name: Chronology
description: The episode's subject laid out in time. Era or date markers become the headers and each carries a short paragraph, so a reader sees the arc of the story before pressing play. Distinct from a chapter list: these mark the subject's timeline, not the video's.
architecture: Dated era markers as headers, a short paragraph under each.

sections.instruction: One paragraph naming the span of time this episode covers and why that span is the right frame for the story. No heading of its own.
Describe the earliest period the episode covers, in one short paragraph. Begin the paragraph with the period or date it concerns, taken from the story context.
Describe the middle period — the point where the situation changes. One short paragraph, again opening with its period or date.
Describe what followed and where things stood by the end of the episode's span. One short paragraph.
Two or three sentences on what remains of this today, or what is still unsettled about it. If the story context does not support a present-day link, describe the unresolved questions instead.
Emit only hashtags, on a single line, separated by spaces. No sentence, no heading, no commentary.

title_plan.guidance: Name the subject and its period. A date or era in the title is welcome. Avoid framing the past as a secret or a thing they hid from you.

tag_plan.guidance: for this chronological episode, mixing the subject, the period, and the place

constraints: Dates and periods come from the story context and are never invented.
Describe each period in its own terms before judging it.
No present-day moralising that replaces explanation.
